H1.statement: The tuned classical baselines match or beat every quantum kernel on this data.
H1.test: AUC with error bars across all configurations.

H2.statement: Geometric difference correlates positively with the quantum-minus-classical AUC gap.
H2.test: Spearman correlation across configurations, with a confidence interval.

H3.statement: As qubits and depth grow at fixed bandwidth, concentration rises and AUC falls.
H3.test: plot variance and AUC against qubit count.

H4.statement: Reducing bandwidth c reduces concentration and recovers performance, while pulling g back toward 1.
H4.test: sweep c at fixed qubits; plot g, variance and AUC together.

provenance: written in the project guide on 7 Nov 2026, before any experiment was run; not formally pre-registered
data: main_grid + big_qubits: PCA, N_train = 500, N_test = 1000, 5 seeds
significance_rule: seed-paired mean difference within one seed-to-seed sd (ddof=1) -> 'not significant'; correlations: 95% bootstrap CI over configurations containing 0 -> 'not significant'

operational_choices.concentration: off-diagonal variance of the training kernel matrix
operational_choices.headline_g: g_lam0.01 (regularised g, as in Fig. 4); lambda = 0, 1e-3, 1e-1 reported alongside
operational_choices.best_classical: max of the three classical models' test AUCs (flatters classical; see robustness bias)

H1.detail: no configuration has a quantum kernel above the best classical baseline by more than the seed spread (fidelity: 58 classical better, 21 not significant, 0 quantum better; projected: 60 / 19 / 0 of 79). Against the RBF-SVM alone, 2 configuration(s) exceed it (~3.6 per kernel expected by chance with this lenient rule)

H2.detail: headline (g_lam0.01): rho = -0.44 [-0.61, -0.22]; all lambdas: lambda=0 -0.50 [-0.65, -0.32], lambda=0.001 -0.63 [-0.74, -0.46], lambda=0.01 -0.44 [-0.61, -0.22], lambda=0.1 +0.34 [+0.09, +0.54]. Only lambda=0.1 is significantly positive, and it vanishes once log kernel variance is controlled for (partial rho +0.03 [-0.19, +0.25]). Significantly NEGATIVE (opposite to H2) at lambda=0, lambda=0.001, lambda=0.01

H3.detail: qubits: variance falls and AUC falls together in 4 of 15 (map, c) cells: ZZ map, reps 1 c=0.25, ZZ map, reps 1 c=0.5, ZZ map, reps 1 c=1, ZZ map, reps 2 c=0.5; variance falls but AUC does not in: Z map, reps 2 c=0.5, Z map, reps 2 c=1, ZZ map, reps 1 c=0.1, ZZ map, reps 2 c=0.1, ZZ map, reps 2 c=0.25, ZZ map, reps 2 c=1 (AUC already at chance from n=4); the remaining cells show no significant variance fall. Depth (ZZ reps 2 vs reps 1, 25 (n, c) cells): reps 2 more concentrated in 12, AUC lower in 14 -- no consistent depth effect

H4.held: FIRST HALF HELD IN PART; SECOND HALF FAILED
H4.first_half: smaller c recovers AUC in 15 of 15 (map, n) cells and raises kernel variance in 8 of 15; variance is NOT raised in Z map, reps 2 n=2, Z map, reps 2 n=4, Z map, reps 2 n=6, Z map, reps 2 n=8, Z map, reps 2 n=10, ZZ map, reps 1 n=2, ZZ map, reps 2 n=2: there the kernel flattens towards a constant at small c, so its variance falls even though AUC recovers
H4.second_half: verdict based on the headline regularised g (lambda=0.01): it falls steadily toward 1 in only 7 of 15 cells; at c=0.05 it is 2.1-4.7, never near 1, and for ZZ maps it peaks at intermediate c. Unregularised g (lambda=0) is closer to 1 at c=0.05 than at c=1 in 15 of 15 cells and falls steadily in 15 of 15, by orders of magnitude, but still ends at 2.8-398 at c=0.05: it moves toward 1 without getting there

H2.gap: fidelity QSVM AUC - best classical AUC (gap_vs_best)

label_aware.definition: log10(s_classical / s_quantum); s = ridge-regularised model complexity (src.metrics.model_complexity, a stand-in for Huang et al.'s s_K(N))
label_aware.note: H2 expects rho > 0. ratio_minus_g is the signed difference of the two Spearman rhos: a CI excluding 0 means the two quantities differ in how they track the gap

bound_regime.interpretation: s = alpha^T K alpha / N equals Huang et al.'s s_K(N)/N, so their bound ~ sqrt(s) is vacuous for s >~ 1. s_classical is never below 1 here, and near-identity (concentrated) quantum kernels get s_quantum ~ 1 because they memorise the labels; the ratio s_C/s_Q therefore mostly flags memorising kernels, which generalise worst. The label-aware test is run outside the regime where the bound means anything.
